applications.label: v9:lem:product
applications.source_location: Chapter IV, Sections 1-3; Proposition VII.2.2, p.191 (proof only for the nonminimal-model extension)
applications.hypotheses: Integral Weierstrass coefficients over the complete DVR of K_v. The formal power series at infinity converges on the maximal ideal.
applications.conventions: Use z=-x/y and w=-1/y. For the fixed integral short model x=z^-2 times a unit, y=-z^-3 times a unit; hence v(x)<0 iff the point belongs to this formal neighborhood.
applications.translation: At 2 no minimal-model theorem is invoked. The integral formal group gives a subgroup directly. It is open, so compactness of the projective curve gives finite index.

applications.label: v9:lem:product
applications.hypotheses: At d=(3-sqrt2), residue field F7; integral model is minimal since v(a4)=2<4, and P reduces to nonsingular (1,6).
applications.conventions: E0 is preimage of the nonsingular locus under reduction of the minimal equation; its image is a group. Thus all multiples of P stay in E0.
applications.translation: Uses subgroup closure only, not an isomorphism E(K_v)=E_ns(F7). Positive x-valuation would reduce to singular (0,0).

applications.label: v9:lem:separation
applications.hypotheses: The selected odd primes are split good-reduction primes, so the opposite reduced curve is elliptic over F_p, not F_(p^2).
applications.conventions: d_+(p) counts all F_p-points including infinity. |d_+(p)-(p+1)|<=2sqrt(p).
applications.translation: Uniform absolute bound with q=p; full rational two-torsion gives4|d_+(p). The integer divisibility argument uses both this and N^(2/3) separation.

applications.label: subsec:v9-deep-completeness
applications.source_location: Proposition IV.5.5; Lemma IV.6.3; Theorem IV.6.4, pp.129-132
applications.hypotheses: K_v/Q_p unramified, p>76176, v(p)=1, formal depth r>=1>1/(p-1).
applications.conventions: log_E is normalized by linear coefficient1, preserves v(z), and is a homomorphism to addition on this disc.
applications.translation: Multiplication by p^19 increases v(log_E) and therefore v(z) by19. The 4r error and G9 tail are separately proved from the manuscript recurrence, not asserted by Silverman.

new_derivations.label: subsec:v9-local-depth

new_derivations.label: v9:lem:separation

new_derivations.label: subsec:v9-deep-completeness

new_derivations.label: subsec:v9-finite

new_derivations.label: subsec:v9-laurent

unlabelled_derivations: Shorter Laurent circuit: e and all denominator powers nonzero by retained norm guard; reversible fixed powers.
Scalar preparation: b(T-t^2)=1 and TV=2 imply nonzero b,T and exactly U=V-b.
Coefficient normalization and eliminations: nonzero rational scales, no variable pivots; original input is fixed.
